strengths: The paper addresses a practically important problem: restoring cross-chunk causal dependencies when reusing prefetched KV caches in RAG, where prefilling dominates inference cost.

The key empirical insight — that prompt-conditioned attention norms are effective for selecting recomputation targets only when computed under an inference-consistent (GLOBAL) RoPE geometry — is a genuinely useful observation, and the four-configuration RoPE ablation (Table 1) cleanly demonstrates the effect.

Evaluation is broad: three LLM backbones and four LongBench tasks under two chunking settings (Table 3), five VLM benchmarks on Qwen3-VL-8B (Table 4), Needle-in-a-Haystack analysis (Fig. 3), and end-to-end latency Pareto analysis (Fig. 2, Table 5) including a favorable comparison against ring attention under sequence parallelism.

The discussion of the 2x overhead from irregular attention masks and the numerical discrepancy analysis between ring attention and single-GPU prefill (Appendix B) reflect honest, technically careful treatment of limitations.
The method is plug-and-play, training-free, and computationally cheap (a simple attention-norm signal from a few intermediate layers), making it easy to adopt.
weaknesses: The 'information flow' framing is oversold relative to the actual mechanism: prompt-to-token attention mass (Eq. 7) is a well-known importance signal (e.g., attention-based eviction in H2O and related work). The contribution is essentially applying this known signal to recomputation target selection plus a RoPE-positioning fix, but the paper presents it as a new principled perspective without formalizing information flow.

The recomputation procedure is under-specified. Recomputing a selected token's KV at its global position across all layers requires a forward pass whose hidden states depend on the mixed set of cached chunk-local and other recomputed states; the exact iterative algorithm, and how attention over partially cached contexts is executed, is not formalized anywhere in the paper or appendix, which hurts reproducibility.

Hyperparameter selection raises evaluation-concern validity issues: the layer range (22–25) was chosen by measuring downstream accuracy on the same benchmarks used for reporting (Appendix B, Fig. 4), and the RoPE-geometry ablation is only run on Qwen. No statistical significance or variance is reported anywhere.

There are unexplained inconsistencies in Table 3: e.g., LLaMA's baseline differs between the 'Fixed Chunk' and 'Passage Split' columns (0.1623 vs 0.1862 on NarrativeQA) even though the baseline should be identical, and No-Recompute (0.2639) exceeds the full-context Baseline (0.1623) on LLaMA NarrativeQA, which is anomalous and unaddressed.

Recompute-budget comparability across methods is not made explicit for the main results: EPIC is fixed at 15%, but the ratio used by 'Ours' and CacheBlend in Table 3 is not stated, weakening the 'comparable efficiency budgets' claim (only Table 5 states 0.15).

The reordering component gives mixed results (e.g., clearly hurts on Qwen fixed-chunk: 0.4773 vs 0.5089 without reorder), so its value and recommended usage are unclear, and the two-stage reselect procedure adds complexity without a dedicated ablation.

The RoPE-similarity analysis (Table 2) is partially circular: it shows that the proposed selection correlates with positional proximity under the geometry the method itself constructs, rather than establishing a causal mechanism; no code release or reproducibility artifacts are mentioned.

strengths: The paper addresses a real and practical problem: the prefilling bottleneck in RAG when reusing independently prefetched chunk KV caches, and it positions itself clearly against CacheBlend and EPIC.

The RoPE geometry ablation (Table 1) is a genuinely interesting empirical finding, showing that token selection quality depends strongly on whether selection-time positional layout matches inference-time decoding (GLOBAL consistently outperforms HL–HP, HL–TP, TL–TP configurations).

The evaluation scope is broad: three LLM backbones (Qwen3-14B, Llama-3.1-8B, GLM-4-9B) on four LongBench QA datasets, plus VLM benchmarks (Table 4), Needle-in-a-Haystack analysis (Appendix A), and a sequence-parallel latency study comparing against ring attention (Tables 5–6).

The Discussion (Section 8) honestly identifies a concrete limitation, namely up to 2x kernel-level overhead from irregular attention masks during recomputation, and correctly frames it as a shared limitation of selective recomputation methods.
The proposed selection signal (aggregated prompt-to-context attention mass, Eq. 7–8) is simple, training-free, and plug-and-play, which is practically appealing.
weaknesses: The 'information flow' framing is oversold relative to the actual method. The core contribution reduces to top-k selection by prompt-to-context attention mass — a signal closely related to well-studied attention-based token importance (e.g., H2O, Quest, retrieval-head literature). The claim that this jointly captures 'semantic relevance and effective information flow' is asserted rhetorically but never formalized or measured as information flow (no causal/graph-theoretic analysis); Table 2's RoPE-similarity analysis is post-hoc and correlational, with modest margins (e.g., MoM 0.5324 vs 0.5243 vs 0.5049 on LLaMA/2WikiMQA).

The method description is ambiguous at a critical point. Token selection is stated to use 'KV states obtained from the prefilling stage' but computed under the GLOBAL RoPE configuration — yet those cached KV states carry chunk-local RoPE. How the prompt-to-context attention matrix in Eq. 7 is actually computed (re-encoding keys under global positions? re-rolling queries only? full forward pass?) is not specified, which materially affects both correctness and the claimed overhead. This is not addressed even in Appendix B.

The reorder component is inconsistent and partially undermines the claims. In Table 3, Our + Reorder substantially degrades over Our in many cells (e.g., Qwen fixed-chunk: 2WikiMQA 0.5089→0.4773, MuSiQue 0.3384→0.2872, HotpotQA 0.5967→0.5053). The text describes reorder as 'maintaining comparable performance' and 'yielding additional gains in several settings,' which does not square with the magnitude of the drops. The two-stage selection (HL–TP then GLOBAL) adds complexity without a clear account of when reordering helps or hurts.

No statistical significance, variance, or seed information is reported, and several results look noisy or anomalous: LLaMA NarrativeQA 'No Recompute' (0.2639) exceeds the full-context baseline (0.1623) in the fixed-chunk column; in passage-split NarrativeQA, EPIC (0.2291) marginally beats Our (0.2288) on Qwen despite the claim of consistent superiority.

Hyperparameter provenance is weak. The layer choice of 22–25 for computing attention norms is tuned on Qwen only and then applied to 'all models,' without justification for how layer indices transfer across architectures of different depths (e.g., Llama-3.1-8B has 32 layers). Figure 4's caption is also mismatched with its content (it describes NIAH heatmaps but shows layer-range score curves).

Efficiency claims require caveats: the sequence-parallel comparison (Table 5) uses a 0.15 recomputation ratio, which is a fairly generous budget, and the TTFT advantage over ring attention is contingent on implementation choices and the observation that most selected tokens fall in the first chunk — a position-dependent artifact that deserves closer analysis.

Gains over CacheBlend, while consistent in direction, are moderate in many cells and the paper lacks ablations isolating the contribution of global positional reconstruction alone versus the attention-norm signal, making it hard to attribute improvements.

No code release or reproducibility statement is provided; given the implementation ambiguity above, independent reproduction would be difficult. Presentation also has rough edges (Section 5 titled 'Ablation Result', typos such as '707.8,ms', highlighting 'best/second-best excluding baseline' in Table 3 which obscures the gap to full-context prefill).

strengths: The core insight is clean and useful: recomputation targets should be selected under the same global RoPE geometry used at inference time, and Table 1 shows this matters substantially (GLOBAL consistently beats HL-HP/TL-TP variants across four benchmarks), which is a non-obvious empirical finding that others can build on.

Broad experimental coverage: three LLM backbones (Qwen3-14B, Llama-3.1-8B, GLM-4-9B), four LongBench datasets under both fixed-chunk and passage-split settings, five VLM benchmarks on Qwen3-VL-8B, Needle-in-a-Haystack analysis (Appendix A), and latency measurements on A100 and 4x H100 with sequence parallelism.

The efficiency analysis is a strength: Table 5 shows competitive or better TTFT versus ring attention at 16K/32K (3.01x/3.49x speedup over single-GPU prefill), and Table 6 shows accuracy gains over ring attention under identical sequence-parallel settings, which supports practical relevance beyond accuracy tables.

The discussion of limitations is reasonably honest: the paper explicitly acknowledges up to 2x recomputation overhead from irregular attention masks being a kernel-level issue shared by all selective recomputation methods, and explains the numerical discrepancy between single-GPU baseline and ring attention (Appendix B).

The RoPE-similarity analysis (Table 2) provides an interesting mechanistic explanation for why attention-norm-selected tokens are positionally reachable, and the layer-wise analysis for norm extraction (Appendix B) adds useful implementation guidance.
weaknesses: The central method is a simple attention-heuristic (top-k by aggregated prompt-to-token attention mass, Eq. 7-8) that is closely related to well-known attention-based importance scores (e.g., H2O-style heuristics), while the 'information flow' framing is largely rhetorical: there is no formal analysis or causal evidence linking the attention-norm score to information flow; the RoPE similarity analysis in Section 5.2 is purely correlational.

The method does not close the gap to the full-context baseline in several settings: e.g., Qwen 2WikiMQA (0.5089 vs 0.5161), LLaMA HotpotQA (0.5150 vs 0.5410), ChatGLM NarrativeQA fixed-chunk (0.3239 vs 0.3264). The paper claims consistent gains 'over prior methods,' but the practical value depends on how much accuracy loss versus full prefill is acceptable, and this trade-off is not always characterized per method (recompute budgets for CacheBlend/EPIC comparisons are not clearly equalized in Table 3).

The reordering contribution is inconsistent: 'Our + Reorder' often underperforms 'Our' (e.g., Qwen fixed-chunk MuSiQue 0.2872 vs 0.3384, HotpotQA 0.5053 vs 0.5967; ChatGLM NarrativeQA 0.3140 vs 0.3239), and no criterion is given for when reordering helps, weakening it as a validated contribution.

No statistical significance testing, variance, or error bars are reported for accuracy results; with a median over 10 runs for latency only, small differences (often ~0.01-0.02 F1) between methods cannot be assessed reliably.

Reproducibility concerns: no code release is mentioned; the norm layer selection (layers 22-25) is tuned on Qwen (32 layers) and then applied to all models including GLM-4-9B, raising questions about whether per-model layer selection is needed and how the method transfers without such tuning; several implementation details (e.g., how the prompt-to-context selection pass avoids full prefill cost, exact recompute budgets per method) are under-specified.

Some VLM results are mixed: at k=2, HRBench4K for 'Our' (0.72625) is below the no-recompute setting (0.72750), and gains elsewhere are modest, which tempers the generality claim for multimodal settings.

strengths: The paper addresses a practical and timely problem: recovering cross-chunk dependencies when independently prefetched KV caches are assembled at inference time in RAG, where full-context prefilling is redundant but causally necessary for accuracy.

The central empirical insight—that token selection must be performed under an inference-consistent RoPE geometry (GLOBAL positioning)—is clearly motivated and convincingly demonstrated by the ablation in Table 1, where mismatched configurations (HL–HP, TL–TP) degrade performance substantially (e.g., 0.2871 vs 0.3386 on MuSiQue).

The evaluation is unusually comprehensive for this area: three LLM backbones and four LongBench tasks under two chunking regimes (Table 3), VLM benchmarks on Qwen3-VL-8B (Table 4), Needle-in-a-Haystack heatmaps (Appendix A), additional baselines including KVLink5, TurboRAG, PCW, BM25-based selection, and KV compression methods (Appendices B and D), an attention-MSE diagnostic (Table 12), layer-selection analysis (Fig. 4), a latency breakdown (Table 14), and an honest discussion of kernel-level overhead for irregular masks (Section 8).

Comparisons are largely fair: all recomputation methods use the same 15% budget, and baseline/no-recompute references are reported alongside. The efficiency analysis (Tables 5-6) shows credible TTFT gains over ring attention at 16K-32K with quality improvements.
The chunk reordering ablation (Appendix E) includes a Descending control, providing evidence that placement near the prompt—rather than reordering per se—drives the effect.

Limitations are treated honestly: the 'information flow' notion is explicitly operational rather than formal, the method's scope (multi-chunk KV reuse, not contexts exceeding the window) is stated, and the up-to-2x kernel overhead of sparse recomputation is acknowledged.
weaknesses: Conceptual novelty is modest. Prompt-conditioned attention mass as a token-importance signal is well established (e.g., SnapKV, Quest-style selection); the main contribution is re-instantiating this signal in the KV-reuse setting plus the RoPE-consistency observation. The 'information flow' framing is largely presentational, and the authors themselves concede it is operational rather than a formal analysis.

There is no statistical rigor: results are single numbers without variance, confidence intervals, or significance tests across seeds. Several anomalies (e.g., Our exceeding the full-context baseline by large margins on NarrativeQA, 0.2288 vs 0.1654) go unexplained and could reflect evaluation noise or metric idiosyncrasies.

The reordering contribution is inconsistent: in fixed-chunk settings, Our+Reorder frequently underperforms Our (Qwen 2WikiMQA 0.4773 vs 0.5089; MuSiQue 0.2872 vs 0.3384), and similar mixed behavior appears for LLaMA. The narrative that reordering 'yields additional gains in several settings' overstates what the tables support, and the two-pass reordering design adds complexity whose benefit is not uniformly demonstrated.

Hyperparameters appear tuned on one model family: layers 22-25 for attention norms were selected via analysis on Qwen3-14B (32 layers) and then applied to all models, without ablation on LLaMA/GLM or justification for how the range transfers across models with different depths.
VLM gains are comparatively small and mixed (at k=2, CacheBlend leads on OCRBench 845 vs 842), so the multimodal generality claim is only partially supported.

Reproducibility is limited: no code or artifact release is mentioned, and key implementation details (FlashInfer-style sparse kernels, two-stage selection pipeline, exact scoring procedure) are spread thinly; independent replication would be nontrivial.

The RoPE-geometry ablation (Table 1) is only conducted on Qwen under the passage-split setting, leaving the generality of the paper's central claim across architectures and chunking regimes unverified.

strengths: The paper addresses a real and timely systems problem (prefilling bottleneck in multi-chunk KV reuse for RAG) and positions itself clearly against CacheBlend and EPIC.

The experimental scope is broad: three LLM backbones (Qwen3-14B, Llama-3.1-8B, GLM-4-9B), a VLM (Qwen3-VL-8B), four LongBench tasks, five VLM benchmarks, Needle-in-a-Haystack, LongBench v2, and additional baselines (KVLink5, TurboRAG, PCW, BM25 Recompute, KV compression methods) in the appendix.

The RoPE geometry ablation (Table 1) and the RoPE-similarity analysis (Table 2) provide genuine insight into why selection under inference-consistent positional assignment matters, which is arguably the paper's most interesting finding.

The efficiency analysis is relatively honest: the discussion section acknowledges up to 2x overhead from irregular attention masks and clarifies that TTFT comparisons reflect kernel-level implementations rather than FLOP counts.
Latency breakdown, Pareto-frontier analysis, and a principled treatment of the ring-attention numerical discrepancy add reproducibility-relevant detail.
weaknesses: Limited originality of the core method: prompt-conditioned attention mass as a token-importance signal is a well-known relevance heuristic; the contribution reduces to applying it in the KV-reuse setting plus a RoPE-consistent geometry choice. The 'information flow' framing is operational and, by the authors' own admission, not a formal analysis, so the conceptual contribution feels thinner than the framing suggests.

The chunk reordering component, one of the stated contributions, yields inconsistent gains: on Qwen fixed-chunk it degrades 2WikiMQA (0.5089 to 0.4773) and MuSiQue (0.3384 to 0.2872) relative to the base method, and the reorder ablation (Table 13) shows Descending actually improves HotpotQA. The paper does not explain when reordering helps versus hurts, weakening the claimed validation of the information-flow perspective.

No statistical significance or variance reporting for any QA results; several margins over CacheBlend/EPIC are small (e.g., VLM OCRBench 842 vs. 845 at k=2, where the proposed method actually loses), making the 'consistent gains' claim hard to assess.

Hyperparameters appear tuned on the evaluation benchmarks: the norm layer selection (layers 22-25) is derived from a Qwen-specific layer sweep on the same tasks used in evaluation, and it is unclear how this transfers to LLaMA/GLM or other architectures.

Reproducibility concerns: no code release or artifact link is mentioned, and the FlashInfer-based sparse-recomputation kernels are nontrivial to reimplement; the method description in Section 4 is high-level on implementation (Appendix F is thin on the recomputation mechanics).

The setting is somewhat narrow: the method is explicitly not intended for contexts exceeding the model window, and its benefit requires amortizable chunk-wise prefilling; the paper acknowledges this but the practical niche (multi-query reuse of identical evidence) is not exercised with a multi-query experiment.

Some baselines appear weakly configured: KV compression baselines (Table 11) perform far below even No Recompute on some datasets, and the retrieval-based BM25 Recompute comparison (Table 10) is a strawman given the methods address different stages.

strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem setting: the multi-chunk KV reuse regime with selective recomputation is precisely scoped, and the paper honestly positions the method as most useful when chunk-wise prefilling can be amortized rather than as a replacement for full-context prefilling.

The core idea is simple, principled, and validated: prompt-conditioned attention-norm scoring under inference-consistent (GLOBAL) RoPE geometry is a plausible criterion for jointly capturing semantic relevance and positional reachability, and the RoPE geometry ablation (Table 1) directly supports the inference-consistency claim.

Comprehensive experimental coverage: three LLM backbones and four LongBench datasets under two chunking regimes (Table 3), five VLM benchmarks on Qwen3-VL-8B (Table 4), plus appendix comparisons against CacheBlend, EPIC, KVLink5, TurboRAG, PCW, BM25-recompute, and KV compression/eviction baselines, along with NIAH heatmaps and LongBench v2.

Multiple mechanism-level analyses strengthen the empirical story: RoPE-similarity statistics (Table 2), attention-pattern MSE recovery relative to full-context attention (Table 12), layer-wise scoring analysis (Fig. 4), and chunk-ordering ablation (Table 13) go beyond end-task numbers.

Honest treatment of limitations: the irregular attention mask / kernel overhead discussion (up to 2x over ideal compute) and the latency breakdown (Table 14) give a realistic picture of where gains come from, and the impact statement is appropriate.
weaknesses: The chunk-reordering component is claimed to provide 'consistent' additional value, but the evidence is mixed: in Table 3, Our + Reorder substantially degrades Our on Qwen fixed-chunk MuSiQue (0.3384 -> 0.2872) and HotpotQA (0.5967 -> 0.5053), and on LLaMA fixed-chunk 2WikiMQA (0.4635 -> 0.4455). The text's description of reordering as 'maintaining comparable performance' oversells an inconsistent component.

No statistical treatment of results: all main tables report single point estimates without variance, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Several reported gaps are small (e.g., VLM OCRBench k=2: 842 vs. 845 against CacheBlend; LongBench v2: 28.89% vs. 26.11% on a 180-sample subset), so robustness of the conclusions is hard to judge.

Anomalous results are not investigated: in Table 3, chunk-wise prefilling with no recomputation sometimes beats the full-context baseline (LLaMA NarrativeQA 0.2639 vs. 0.1862; ChatGLM passage-split 0.3181 vs. 0.3264), which is counterintuitive and suggests baseline instability, evaluation noise, or prompt-sensitivity issues that the paper does not discuss.

The 'information flow' framing is somewhat inflated relative to the actual mechanism, which is a top-k selection by summed prompt-to-token attention mass. The paper acknowledges the operational definition, but the narrative (structural propagation under the causal attention graph) goes beyond what is measured; the RoPE-similarity analysis is correlational rather than causal evidence.

Some hyperparameter generality concerns: the scoring layers (22-25) are tuned on Qwen (32 layers) and applied to all models of differing depths; generalization of this choice across architectures is asserted but not ablated per-model.

Scoring depends on prompt-conditioned attention over the full context, which requires a forward pass whose cost partially overlaps with what the method aims to avoid; the latency breakdown shows prefill still dominates (64% of TTFT), so the practical benefit over full prefilling hinges on amortization assumptions that are only realized in the prepared-context or multi-GPU settings.

No code or artifact release is mentioned, which limits reproducibility for a systems-oriented method whose efficiency claims depend on implementation choices (FlashInfer-style sparse kernels, layer choices, chunking). Minor presentation issues remain (e.g., hyphenation artifacts like 'se- lects', 'ap- proach').
